title: Expanding the scope of protein language modeling to protein-protein interactions with MSA Pairformer.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the full GitHub repo tree (yoakiyama/MSA_Pairformer): source code, figure-reproduction notebooks and scripts only. No data tables, no benchmark label files. data_downloader.py only fetches PDB / AlphaFold structures by ID. The Hugging Face model card (yoakiyama/MSA-Pairformer) is public and not gated, about 2 GB of weight files. The README licence is a modified MIT licence, free for commercial use.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: No full text in Europe PMC (no PMCID, paywalled). Benchmark numbers (median interface P@K 0.52 vs MSA Transformer 0.19; CASP15 long-range precision 0.66 vs 0.50 for ESM2-15B; P@K = precision of the top K predicted contacts) come from search snippets of the bioRxiv/Cell abstract. No supplement and no repository accessions were found.

a1_downloadable.note: Code and weights download without a login (checked the GitHub tree and the Hugging Face API). But no dataset is deposited.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No label table exists. Contact labels would have to be computed from PDB structures, and interaction labels (toxin-antitoxin, HK-RR = histidine kinase-response regulator pairs) built by pairing MSAs (multiple sequence alignments). The target must be constructed. Checked in the repo, which contains no data files.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are MSAs that must be generated with MMseqs2/ColabFold searches or pulled from OpenProteinSet/ProteinGym. None are in the repo.

a5_enough_rows.note: No labelled table, so no row count could be checked.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: about 2 GB of weights plus MSAs
a6_fits_laptop.note: The 111M-parameter model would run inference on CPU, slowly with deep MSAs. Not verified.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nothing to compare: no released dataset.

a8_label_provenance.note: Benchmark contacts would come from experimental PDB structures, which is fine in principle. But they are computed by us, not supplied.

existing_models.name: MSA Pairformer (this paper)
existing_models.score_and_split: Median interface-contact P@K (precision of the top K predicted contacts) 0.52 vs 0.19 for MSA Transformer. CASP15 long-range contact precision 0.66 (per search snippets of the abstract).

existing_models.name: MSA Transformer
existing_models.score_and_split: 0.19 median interface P@K and 0.50 CASP15 long-range precision, as reported by the MSA Pairformer authors.

existing_models.name: ESM2-15B, a protein language model
existing_models.score_and_split: 0.50 CASP15 long-range precision, as reported by the MSA Pairformer authors.

backbone.name: MSA Pairformer itself (111M parameters)
backbone.hardware: CPU possible for shallow MSAs; GPU preferred

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: None: the paper releases a model, not a dataset to join.

honest_claim_h3: No dataset-based claim is possible. This paper is a candidate backbone (a pretrained model to reuse) for other projects, not a project dataset.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use paired protein sequence alignments to predict which residues touch across two interacting proteins.
plain_idea.train_on: Paired alignments of interacting protein families. We would have to build these ourselves; the number of examples is unknown.
plain_idea.predict: Residue-residue contacts at the interface between two proteins, with the true answer computed from experimental PDB structures.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Structural biologists screening possible protein partners would get cheaper interface predictions. But this paper already does this task and releases no labelled data.

more_or_better_data.why: We would have no new data. The paper releases only code and weights.

confidence_score.why: No replicate measurements or labelled data to calibrate a confidence score against.

models_beatable.why: MSA Pairformer (2026, open weights) reports roughly a 3-fold gain over MSA Transformer on interface contacts. It is new and strong.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No new data that joins to it measures the same quantity.

ml_idea: None as a standalone project. Record MSA Pairformer as an open, commercially usable, 111M-parameter backbone that could embed MSAs for protein-protein interaction or variant-effect projects (e.g. as features alongside ESM-2 on ProteinGym).

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: there is no dataset to build a table from.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: List the GitHub repo for data files. Done: none found.

verdict_reason: A2/A3 fail. This is a model paper: the repo has only code, notebooks and weights, with no labelled data. Labels would have to be built from PDB structures and alignments generated by us. Worth noting as an open, MIT-style backbone for other protein projects.
